memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Her father will say to the elders, "I gave my daughter in marriage to this man, but he dislikes her. Now he has slandered her and said, 'I did not find your daughter to be a virgin.' But here is the proof of my daughter's virginity." Then her parents shall display the cloth before the elders of the town, and the elders shall take the man and punish him. They shall fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give them to the young woman's father, because this man has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She shall continue to be his wife; he must not divorce her as long as he lives. - Deut 22:16-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The case continues, and we see God's justice at work for the wronged woman. When the false accusation was exposed, the lying husband was punished, fined heavily, and forbidden ever to divorce her. The woman who had been slandered was protected and provided for, and her accuser bore the consequences of his lies. God ensured that the one who tried to destroy an innocent woman's reputation did not get away with it.

Look at how thoroughly God defends the vulnerable here. The slandered woman receives lasting protection, and the man who wronged her faces real accountability. In a world where a woman's word might easily be dismissed, God's law weighted heavily against those who would falsely shame the innocent. This is the justice of a God who lifts up the lowly and defends the defenceless.

This gives us great confidence in the character of God. He is not indifferent to those who are wronged, slandered, or crushed by the powerful. He is a defender of the vulnerable and a God of justice who will ultimately vindicate the innocent. While human courts are imperfect, God's justice is perfect and sure. He calls His people, too, to care about justice for the wronged (Mic 6:8). If you have been mistreated, entrust yourself to the God who judges justly, He sees, He cares, and He will act. Do you trust God as the defender of the wronged?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust God to defend you when you are wronged?
2. How does God's justice for the vulnerable shape your view of Him?
3. How can you stand up for those who are mistreated?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You defend the wronged and lift up the lowly. Help me entrust my hurts to You and stand for justice for others. Amen.
